targetTask: Given an already supplied COBOL and Java pair, detect a reproduced behavioral mismatch and rank the responsible Java locations and constrained repair candidates.
excludedTasks: prediction of mathematical equivalence without a valid proof
learning syntax/compiler failure detection and reporting it as semantic-defect detection

evidenceUnit.unit: independent original defect/issue family, with affected programs and version pairs nested inside it

labels.REPRODUCED_BEHAVIORAL_DEFECT: Same COBOL/input contract; Java builds but disagrees with the reference/regression oracle. Fixed Java resolves the disagreement under that same oracle.
labels.TEST_COMPATIBLE_CONTROL: Builds and passes the declared finite oracle. This label is test-scoped and does not assert universal equivalence or absence of other bugs.
labels.UNRESOLVED: Missing reference/source/runtime context, inconsistent execution, unreviewed defect status or unsupported oracle; not silently labeled correct.
labels.SYNTAX_OR_SETUP_FAILURE: Retain separately for coverage reporting; exclude from the semantic classifier target.

admissionRules: Use naturally occurring reviewed failures; this proposed corpus contains no new injected mutations.
Reproduce before-fix failure and after-fix pass with exact pinned artifacts and unchanged oracle.
Confirm the case is a translation defect under the supported contract, not a new feature, business-policy change or original COBOL bug.
Record the review type faithfully: maintainer approval, researcher defect annotation and independent local adjudication are distinct evidence.
Require relevant dependency/runtime source in model inputs if the defect is invisible in generated Java alone; otherwise exclude with reason.
Keep affected program, all versions, repair attempts, related tests and near-duplicates in the same independent group.
Pair fault/fix cases with unaffected controls generated by both compiler versions to reduce compiler-version/style shortcuts.
Separate source-profile, project and target-language domains; no cross-language-transfer score is called COBOL-to-Java accuracy.
Do not treat multiple annotations or multiple regression assertions from one issue as independent defects.
Admit localization targets only with validated source spans and a reviewed fault location; attention weights and changed compiler lines are not defect-location gold labels.

splitProtocol.existing23ReservedTasks: Remain excluded from all new fitting and selection. They have no reviewed defect labels and cannot alone evaluate the new task.
splitProtocol.crossCorpusOverlap: Audit original problem IDs, repository lineage, language variants and near-duplicates. In particular, EvalPlus/HumanEval in external corpora can overlap the existing143 tasks and their23 reserved families.
splitProtocol.development: Group by original defect/issue family and project. Fit vocabularies, preprocessing, calibration and thresholds inside each training fold only.
splitProtocol.test: Freeze an independently reviewed COBOL-to-Java defect cohort before model/hyperparameter selection. Determine its size after counting eligible independent groups; do not manufacture23 cases from a few issues.
splitProtocol.kPolicy: Choose k from eligible independent groups and class coverage. Five-fold CV is not automatic merely because the old retrieval experiment used it; tiny cohorts support exploratory case studies only.
splitProtocol.freeze: Pin corpus IDs/hashes, label definitions, split, model candidates, metrics and stopping/threshold rules before final scoring.

primary: false-negative rate and false-positive rate at a development-selected operating point
secondary: PR-AUC for the stated class prevalence
source localization Top1/Top3 among cases with reviewed location labels
verified repair success under an unchanged contract and fixed candidate budget
checker invocations and time per validated repair
reporting: uncertainty grouped by issue family when cohort size supports it
raw total, supported, abstained and excluded case counts; do not hide them by reporting only successful supported cases
baselines: Java-only defect detector with the same training information
compiler-version/style or metadata baseline for confounding checks
existing symbolic checker on its supported subset, with coverage reported
learned localization/repair ranking compared with unranked candidates at the same checker-call budget
measurements.ablation: Test whether access to the correct COBOL counterpart improves results over Java-only and shuffled-COBOL inputs; do not infer cross-language reasoning from an accuracy number alone.

claimLimits: Passing finite tests is not proof of arbitrary source equivalence.
A symbolic proof applies only to its explicit supported profile and contract.
The active v4 retrieval metrics remain historical correspondence evidence, not defect-detection accuracy.
No defect-model accuracy can be reported until eligible data, labels and a frozen evaluation exist.
aiDisclosure: AI-generated proposed protocol; no reviewer votes, case reproductions, labels or accuracy statistics are fabricated.
